result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Channel.recv_batch_async()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | pymizu description: Receive up to n values as one list on an asyncio.Future. twitter-card: title: >- [Channel.recv_batch_async()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | pymizu description: Receive up to n values as one list on an asyncio.Future. title: >- [Channel.recv_batch_async()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Receive up to n values as one list on an asyncio.Future. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Receive up to ``n`` values as one list on an `asyncio.Future`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/shikokuchuo/pymizu/blob/main/python/pymizu/__init__.py#L453-L525){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Channel.recv_batch_async(n=256) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The burst form of [`recv_async()`](`pymizu.Channel.recv_async`): one Future resolves with a whole burst of arrivals at once, the high-throughput receive form — one resolution per burst rather than one per message. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[256]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The maximum batch size. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ An `asyncio.Future` resolving with a list of up to ``n``]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : values in arrival order — possibly short: it resolves as soon as at least one value is available, never waiting to fill. Terminal states stay values: the Future resolves with the `CLOSED` / `PEER_GONE` sentinel. An ``n`` past the drain quantum (2048) resolves with at most one quantum per pass. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ``n`` is less than 1. [ConcurrentUseError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A blocking receive on this side from another thread races the armed async consumer: a side is confined to one thread and one consumer form at a time. ::: ## Details {.doc-details} Outstanding calls on one channel — [`recv_async()`](`pymizu.Channel.recv_async`) singles and batch waiters mixed — resolve in call order, each batch waiter taking up to its ``n`` from the burst (at least one when it is reached, so a batch reached late in a busy pass can resolve short). Cancelling the Future detaches the waiter, and the next message goes to the next waiter. There is no ``timeout`` argument: use `asyncio.timeout` or `asyncio.wait_for`. A channel created with ``spin=True`` cannot arm and raises. The async consumer is the side's one consumer: a blocking [`recv()`](`pymizu.Channel.recv`) on the same side while waiters are pending raises [`ConcurrentUseError`](`pymizu.ConcurrentUseError`). A declined foreign payload (see [`recv_async()`](`pymizu.Channel.recv_async`)) ahead of a batch resolves it short with the values before it; the waiter that reaches the declined message rejects with [`ForeignPayloadError`](`pymizu.ForeignPayloadError`), and the consumer keeps flowing. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#b6e5e5c9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pymizu with pymizu.Channel.create(''' import pymizu while True: x = ch.recv() if x is pymizu.CLOSED: break ch.send(x) ''') as ch: ch.send_batch([1, 2, 3]) batch = await ch.recv_batch_async() batch ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 3] ``` ::: :::
